# mlvtoolbox

Documentation and articles: <https://bbuchsbaum.github.io/mlvtoolboxR/>

`mlvtoolbox` is an R package for measuring contour geometry and
constructing reproducible visual stimuli from line drawings. It is an
independently maintained R port and extension of the Bernhardt-Walther
Lab’s [Mid-Level Vision
Toolbox](https://github.com/bwlabToronto/MLV_toolbox), with
[pyMLV](https://github.com/bwlabToronto/pyMLV) as an additional
reference.

The aim is to make the [original MLV
methods](https://doi.org/10.3389/fcomp.2023.1140723) available in R with
explicit measurement choices, tested native performance improvements,
and tools for matching stimulus sets. Where this package defines a
measure differently from the original toolbox, for example so that
junctions and branch scores do not depend on contour direction or on the
start vertex of a closed contour, or so that each curvature turn is
counted once, the package definition is the default and the published
behaviour remains available through explicit `mlv2023` options. Each
difference is recorded, with a reproducer, in the [differences
register](https://bbuchsbaum.github.io/mlvtoolboxR/DIFFERENCES.md).
Graph/design workflows are named extensions. Numerical equivalence is
qualified against specific fixtures, not promised for every upstream
output.

[Purpose and
differences](https://bbuchsbaum.github.io/mlvtoolboxR/docs/ATTRIBUTION.md)
· [Credits and license
audit](https://bbuchsbaum.github.io/mlvtoolboxR/vendor/LICENSING.md) ·
[Measurement
contract](https://bbuchsbaum.github.io/mlvtoolboxR/docs/FEATURE_SPEC.md)

## Install locally

A C++17 compiler and Rcpp are required. From this repository:

``` r

install.packages("Rcpp")
install.packages(".", repos = NULL, type = "source")
```

Optional packages: xml2 for SVG, R.matlab for v5 MAT files, and png/jpeg
for images. Python, Octave and model weights are not runtime
dependencies.

## Drawing to features

Contours are ordered matrices with columns x1, y1, x2, y2. Image
coordinates increase rightward/downward; integer raster pixel centers
start at (1,1). Subpixel coordinates are retained. Zero-length segments
require explicit cleaning with zero_length=“drop”.

``` r

library(mlvtoolbox)
drawing <- mlv_drawing(
  list(rbind(c(5, 5, 35, 5), c(35, 5, 35, 25)),
       matrix(c(20, 1, 20, 30), nrow = 1)),
  width = 40, height = 35
)
drawing <- compute_contour_properties(drawing)
as.data.frame(drawing)             # segment measurements
drawing$junctions                  # positions, types, arms and angles
contour_statistics(drawing)        # long image-level histograms
feature_table(drawing)             # normalized contour-level predictors
plot_properties(drawing)
```

Histogram weighting and normalization are explicit:
orientation/curvature collect segment length; length collects
whole-contour length; junctions count events. A value within 1e-9 ×
max(1, \|edge\|) of a bin edge is binned as if on the edge, so
mathematically equal angles share a bin on every platform. Normalized
values are per 10,000 contour pixels. Valid zero scores remain distinct
from missing scores.

## How this port differs

- **An R workflow:** drawing objects, feature tables and model
  compatibility metadata; Python and MATLAB serve as references.
- **Explicit method definitions:** subpixel geometry, validated
  degeneracies and missingness, vertex-turning curvature by default
  (each turn counted once), an arc-length estimator at a stated scale,
  and physical calibration. `estimator = "mlv2023"` retains the
  published curvature.
- **Additional stimulus tools:** constrained subset design and contour
  graph descriptors for closure, continuation and enclosure.
- **Measured implementation changes:** compiled geometry and fused
  histograms, with [performance and equality
  evidence](https://bbuchsbaum.github.io/mlvtoolboxR/docs/FUSED_STATISTICS.md).
- **Two modes for curvature, junctions and the medial axis:** the
  package defaults, and explicit `mlv2023` options that reproduce
  outputs the original lab computed in MATLAB (see [parity
  evidence](https://bbuchsbaum.github.io/mlvtoolboxR/docs/PARITY.md)).
  No bundled SAM weights or MATLAB serialized models.

See the [comparison with the
originals](https://bbuchsbaum.github.io/mlvtoolboxR/docs/ATTRIBUTION.md)
for scope, source lineage and qualification boundaries.

## Medial-axis analysis

``` r

mask <- rasterize(drawing)
result <- analyse_mat(drawing, min_branch_points = 2)
plot(result$drawing, property = "parallelism")
scores <- contour_statistics(result$drawing, properties = "parallelism")
rgb <- render_drawing(result$drawing, property = "parallelism")
```

compute_mat() returns distances, nearest-boundary indices, AOF,
skeleton, ordered branches, and method parameters.
compute_mat_properties() adds parallelism, separation, mirror and
optional taper ratings. map_mat_properties() transfers them back to
contours.

By default the flux is pixel-centred and independent of how equidistant
boundary pixels are labelled, the skeleton keeps no removable pixel, and
branch scores do not depend on branch direction or numbering. The
published-compatible recipe reproduces the lab’s stored MATLAB results:
on 2,757 drawings, 99.1–99.4% of per-pixel scores agree within 1e-4
(residual: MATLAB’s single precision).

``` r

compat <- compute_mat(drawing, aof = "mlv2023", morphology = "hmt8",
                      branch_rule = "mlv2023",
                      threshold_angle = asin(0.3 * pi / 2) * 180 / pi)
```

These comparisons qualify computation against stored outputs, not the
perceptual validity of the measures. See [parity
evidence](https://bbuchsbaum.github.io/mlvtoolboxR/docs/PARITY.md) and
[implementation
status](https://bbuchsbaum.github.io/mlvtoolboxR/IMPLEMENTATION_STATUS.md).

## Manipulate and import

``` r

parts <- split_contours(drawing, property = "curvature", fraction = 0.5)
rotated <- rotate_drawing(drawing, 30)
clipped <- clip_circle(rotated, radius = 15)
segmented <- segment_at_junctions(drawing)
regions <- split_junction_regions(drawing)

# Optional file adapters:
# drawing <- read_mlv_svg("drawing.svg")
# drawings <- read_mlv_mat("drawings.mat")
# traced <- trace_contours("black_lines_on_white.png")
# write_mlv_png(drawing, "drawing.png")
```

Both ranked groups obey their requested whole-contour length budgets; a
middle contour can remain unassigned. Curvature means and integrated
curvature have separate names. Geometry-changing operations invalidate
derived results.

Model scoring accepts an R model/predict method or a function of a
feature table. Bind the exact training table’s measurement schema before
prediction:

``` r

features <- feature_table(drawing)
model <- bind_feature_model(function(z) z$length_1, features)
scores <- predict_contours(drawing, model)
```

The schema records predictor order, bin edges, weights, units and
normalization. Prediction rejects missing or incompatible training
metadata before calling the model. Use fixed `length_range` and
`curvature_range` values when comparing drawings with different canvas
sizes. A model can instead receive its training schema via
`expected_spec = feature_schema(features)`. The explicit legacy option
`check_spec = FALSE` warns that compatibility was not checked.

trace_rgb() requires an explicitly supplied provider returning an ink
mask; xdog_lines() is the built-in classical provider (a flow-based
difference of Gaussians, the [Line
extraction](https://bbuchsbaum.github.io/mlvtoolboxR/articles/line-extraction.html)
article). No SAM model/backend is bundled; arbitrary edge detectors are
not silently substituted for SAM. MATLAB serialized regression models,
general SVG paint effects and MAT v7.3/HDF5 import are outside the
current adapters.

For reproducible measurements, use a fixed specification:

``` r

spec <- feature_spec(c("length", "curvature", "orientation"),
                     estimator = "arclength", curvature_scale = 2)
measured <- compute_contour_properties(drawing, spec = spec)
features <- feature_table(measured)
```

The default curvature estimator, `turning`, spreads each vertex turn
over the half-segments on either side of it, so every turn is counted
once; `arclength` smooths the turns at a stated scale. Both wrap closed
contours. The published estimator, `estimator = "mlv2023"`, counts the
last vertex of every contour twice and depends on how a curve is
sampled; use it to reproduce published values. Physical measurement uses
`units = "visual_degrees"` with an explicit `pixels_per_degree`. New
branch scores use `branch_estimator = "arclength"`. See the [measurement
contract](https://bbuchsbaum.github.io/mlvtoolboxR/docs/FEATURE_SPEC.md)
for definitions, migration, metadata, and the limits of raster
resolution invariance.

## Differences, provenance and storage

- [Differences from the reference
  implementations](https://bbuchsbaum.github.io/mlvtoolboxR/DIFFERENCES.md):
  stable IDs, executed reproducers, source findings and R regressions.
  No upstream reports have been submitted.
- [Source
  provenance](https://bbuchsbaum.github.io/mlvtoolboxR/vendor/SOURCES.json):
  pinned source-only snapshots, retained-file checksums and
  reference-data custody.
- [Cleanup
  receipt](https://bbuchsbaum.github.io/mlvtoolboxR/CLEANUP_RECEIPT.json):
  one verified shared collection at reference-data/mlv; about 2.63 GiB
  of logical duplicate/history storage removed.
- tools/restore_upstream.py restores full original checkouts to an
  explicit new destination. Large reference data and vendor snapshots
  are excluded from the R package tarball.

## Credits, citation and licenses

The original toolbox and methods are by **Dirk Bernhardt-Walther,
Delaram Farzanfar, Seohee Han, Morteza Rezanejad and the
Bernhardt-Walther Lab**. The R implementation and extensions are by
**Bradley Buchsbaum**. We also credit **Aravind Narayanan** for the
Python AOF reference, **Josep Mones i Teixidor and Carnë Draug** for the
Octave morphology tables, and **Peter Kovesi** for retained edge-linking
reference helpers. [Full source and contribution
details](https://bbuchsbaum.github.io/mlvtoolboxR/docs/ATTRIBUTION.md)
distinguish these roles.

Run `citation("mlvtoolbox")` to cite the R implementation and original
methods. The R implementation is declared **GPL-3.0-or-later**; see
[COPYING](https://bbuchsbaum.github.io/mlvtoolboxR/COPYING). [Upstream
notices](https://bbuchsbaum.github.io/mlvtoolboxR/inst/LICENSES) and
[credits](https://bbuchsbaum.github.io/mlvtoolboxR/inst/COPYRIGHTS) are
also included in the installed package.

Vendored sources retain their own terms: Python has an MIT root license
with GPL notices in three files, while many MATLAB files have **no
explicit license grant**. [The
audit](https://bbuchsbaum.github.io/mlvtoolboxR/vendor/LICENSING.md)
records this unresolved permission issue; our GPL declaration does not
relicense those files. Dataset and model redistribution rights are
separate, and neither is asserted here.

## Development

Run testthat::test_local() for behavior/numerical checks. The reference
generation and upstream reproducer scripts are in tools/reference and
tools/upstream. Local check results, benchmarks and cross-platform
status are recorded separately.

For a bounded source build/check, use `python3 tools/bounded_check.py`.
It stages only package files before invoking R, so retained reference
data are not copied into the build workspace.

# Package index

## All functions

- [`analyse_mat()`](https://bbuchsbaum.github.io/mlvtoolboxR/reference/analyse_mat.md)
  : Complete vector drawing to medial-axis feature workflow
- [`as.data.frame(`*`<mlv_contour_graph>`*`)`](https://bbuchsbaum.github.io/mlvtoolboxR/reference/as.data.frame.mlv_contour_graph.md)
  : Export graph spans as a data frame
- [`as.data.frame(`*`<mlv_drawing>`*`)`](https://bbuchsbaum.github.io/mlvtoolboxR/reference/as.data.frame.mlv_drawing.md)
  : Drawing segment table
- [`as_mlv_drawing()`](https://bbuchsbaum.github.io/mlvtoolboxR/reference/as_mlv_drawing.md)
  : Convert an upstream MATLAB drawing representation
- [`average_outward_flux()`](https://bbuchsbaum.github.io/mlvtoolboxR/reference/average_outward_flux.md)
  : Average outward flux of a signed-distance/nearest-boundary field
- [`average_property()`](https://bbuchsbaum.github.io/mlvtoolboxR/reference/average_property.md)
  : Mean geometric or medial-axis property
- [`batch_statistics()`](https://bbuchsbaum.github.io/mlvtoolboxR/reference/batch_statistics.md)
  : Summarize a collection of drawings
- [`bind_feature_model()`](https://bbuchsbaum.github.io/mlvtoolboxR/reference/bind_feature_model.md)
  : Bind a prediction model to its training feature schema
- [`clip_circle()`](https://bbuchsbaum.github.io/mlvtoolboxR/reference/clip_circle.md)
  : Clip all segment-circle intersections
- [`colour_key()`](https://bbuchsbaum.github.io/mlvtoolboxR/reference/colour_key.md)
  : Draw a colour key in its own panel
- [`compute_contour_properties()`](https://bbuchsbaum.github.io/mlvtoolboxR/reference/compute_contour_properties.md)
  : Compute contour measurements and junctions
- [`compute_mat()`](https://bbuchsbaum.github.io/mlvtoolboxR/reference/compute_mat.md)
  : Construct an AOF medial-axis representation
- [`compute_mat_properties()`](https://bbuchsbaum.github.io/mlvtoolboxR/reference/compute_mat_properties.md)
  : Compute medial-axis symmetry scores
- [`contour_graph()`](https://bbuchsbaum.github.io/mlvtoolboxR/reference/contour_graph.md)
  : Construct a contour arrangement and relationship graph
- [`contour_statistics()`](https://bbuchsbaum.github.io/mlvtoolboxR/reference/contour_statistics.md)
  : Histograms of drawing and contour properties
- [`contour_turning()`](https://bbuchsbaum.github.io/mlvtoolboxR/reference/contour_turning.md)
  : Exact signed and absolute vertex turning
- [`curvature_profile()`](https://bbuchsbaum.github.io/mlvtoolboxR/reference/curvature_profile.md)
  : Piecewise exact polygon turning-density profiles
- [`design_subsets()`](https://bbuchsbaum.github.io/mlvtoolboxR/reference/design_subsets.md)
  : Design two matched conditions from whole contours
- [`detect_junctions()`](https://bbuchsbaum.github.io/mlvtoolboxR/reference/detect_junctions.md)
  : Detect and classify intersections between distinct contours
- [`distance_transform()`](https://bbuchsbaum.github.io/mlvtoolboxR/reference/distance_transform.md)
  : Exact Euclidean distance to the nearest feature pixel
- [`draw_mat_axis()`](https://bbuchsbaum.github.io/mlvtoolboxR/reference/draw_mat_axis.md)
  : Add the medial axis to a plot
- [`extract_lines()`](https://bbuchsbaum.github.io/mlvtoolboxR/reference/extract_lines.md)
  : Extract a line drawing from an image
- [`feature_density()`](https://bbuchsbaum.github.io/mlvtoolboxR/reference/feature_density.md)
  : Feature density on a pixel grid
- [`feature_schema()`](https://bbuchsbaum.github.io/mlvtoolboxR/reference/feature_schema.md)
  : Inspect the measurement schema of a feature table
- [`feature_spec()`](https://bbuchsbaum.github.io/mlvtoolboxR/reference/feature_spec.md)
  : Declare a reusable measurement specification
- [`feature_table()`](https://bbuchsbaum.github.io/mlvtoolboxR/reference/feature_table.md)
  : Wide per-contour feature table
- [`fit_line_segments()`](https://bbuchsbaum.github.io/mlvtoolboxR/reference/fit_line_segments.md)
  : Greedy line fitting for ordered points
- [`graph_features()`](https://bbuchsbaum.github.io/mlvtoolboxR/reference/graph_features.md)
  : Summarize topology and geometric contour relations
- [`labels_to_edges()`](https://bbuchsbaum.github.io/mlvtoolboxR/reference/labels_to_edges.md)
  : Convert segmentation labels to an ink boundary mask
- [`line_extraction_stages()`](https://bbuchsbaum.github.io/mlvtoolboxR/reference/line_extraction_stages.md)
  : Intermediate images of the line extractor
- [`map_mat_properties()`](https://bbuchsbaum.github.io/mlvtoolboxR/reference/map_mat_properties.md)
  : Map branch ratings back to drawing contours
- [`mlv_drawing()`](https://bbuchsbaum.github.io/mlvtoolboxR/reference/mlv_drawing.md)
  : Construct a vectorized line drawing
- [`plot(`*`<mlv_drawing>`*`)`](https://bbuchsbaum.github.io/mlvtoolboxR/reference/plot.mlv_drawing.md)
  : Plot vector contours or properties
- [`plot(`*`<mlv_mat>`*`)`](https://bbuchsbaum.github.io/mlvtoolboxR/reference/plot.mlv_mat.md)
  : Plot a stage of a medial-axis representation
- [`plot_branch_profile()`](https://bbuchsbaum.github.io/mlvtoolboxR/reference/plot_branch_profile.md)
  : Plot branch quantities under the drawing they come from
- [`plot_properties()`](https://bbuchsbaum.github.io/mlvtoolboxR/reference/plot_properties.md)
  : Plot several property panels
- [`predict_contours()`](https://bbuchsbaum.github.io/mlvtoolboxR/reference/predict_contours.md)
  : Predict one score per contour
- [`rasterize()`](https://bbuchsbaum.github.io/mlvtoolboxR/reference/rasterize.md)
  : Render a drawing into an ink mask
- [`read_mlv_image()`](https://bbuchsbaum.github.io/mlvtoolboxR/reference/read_mlv_image.md)
  : Read an image as a numeric array
- [`read_mlv_mat()`](https://bbuchsbaum.github.io/mlvtoolboxR/reference/read_mlv_mat.md)
  : Read MATLAB v5 vector drawing structures
- [`read_mlv_svg()`](https://bbuchsbaum.github.io/mlvtoolboxR/reference/read_mlv_svg.md)
  : Import vector contours from SVG
- [`render_drawing()`](https://bbuchsbaum.github.io/mlvtoolboxR/reference/render_drawing.md)
  : Render a drawing with property or model-score colors
- [`rotate_drawing()`](https://bbuchsbaum.github.io/mlvtoolboxR/reference/rotate_drawing.md)
  : Rotate a drawing in image coordinates
- [`score_branch()`](https://bbuchsbaum.github.io/mlvtoolboxR/reference/score_branch.md)
  : Score one skeletal branch
- [`segment_at_junctions()`](https://bbuchsbaum.github.io/mlvtoolboxR/reference/segment_at_junctions.md)
  : Split contours at detected junction positions
- [`shift_contours()`](https://bbuchsbaum.github.io/mlvtoolboxR/reference/shift_contours.md)
  : Shift contours, optionally sampling translations within the image
- [`simplify_contours()`](https://bbuchsbaum.github.io/mlvtoolboxR/reference/simplify_contours.md)
  : Simplify ordered contours by line fitting
- [`skeletonize()`](https://bbuchsbaum.github.io/mlvtoolboxR/reference/skeletonize.md)
  : Thin a binary image
- [`split_by_histogram()`](https://bbuchsbaum.github.io/mlvtoolboxR/reference/split_by_histogram.md)
  : Split contours using weighted feature histograms
- [`split_contours()`](https://bbuchsbaum.github.io/mlvtoolboxR/reference/split_contours.md)
  : Split ranked contours under a whole-contour length budget
- [`split_junction_regions()`](https://bbuchsbaum.github.io/mlvtoolboxR/reference/split_junction_regions.md)
  : Separate middle halves from end quarters
- [`subset_contours()`](https://bbuchsbaum.github.io/mlvtoolboxR/reference/subset_contours.md)
  : Select contours and invalidate derived properties
- [`trace_contours()`](https://bbuchsbaum.github.io/mlvtoolboxR/reference/trace_contours.md)
  : Trace contours from an ink mask or grayscale line drawing
- [`trace_rgb()`](https://bbuchsbaum.github.io/mlvtoolboxR/reference/trace_rgb.md)
  : Trace RGB images with an explicit extraction provider
- [`trace_skeleton()`](https://bbuchsbaum.github.io/mlvtoolboxR/reference/trace_skeleton.md)
  : Trace ordered medial-axis branches
- [`validate_feature_spec()`](https://bbuchsbaum.github.io/mlvtoolboxR/reference/validate_feature_spec.md)
  : Validate a feature specification
- [`write_feature_csv()`](https://bbuchsbaum.github.io/mlvtoolboxR/reference/write_feature_csv.md)
  : Export image or contour statistics
- [`write_mlv_png()`](https://bbuchsbaum.github.io/mlvtoolboxR/reference/write_mlv_png.md)
  : Export a drawing or image to PNG
- [`xdog_lines()`](https://bbuchsbaum.github.io/mlvtoolboxR/reference/xdog_lines.md)
  : Line extraction as a trace_rgb() backend
